item.title: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
Timer expired, edits made.

The WikiWalk team is proposing edits to this page. All proposed edits will be in a collapsible below this post, and after 7 days if there are no serious objections to the edits, the feedback received will be taken into account as the edits are made. If you have questions not directly related to the article about this project, please pm a member of the WikiWalk Team.

+ show block
- hide block

In the comment section of this article, SCP-1427 is brought up because it too defines an EK-class scenario, in which "Catastrophic containment failure is predicted to constitute a EK-class event, resulting in the extinguishment of all human consciousness within approximately 215 days." The author of this article replied to say the two could work so long as the EK-class scenario wasn't instantaneous, but as seen in SCP-1427, the build up to the scenario is not immediate, taking 215 days to afflict every human being. Upon speaking with Drewbear, they said the intended meaning for an EK-Class scenario in this article means that humanity has "no chance" of recovering from it, which is similar to what we see in SCP-1427. Taking this into consideration, recommending the following change:

Editing this:

The broadcast at 100.2 MHz is apparently a looped recording of survival instructions, rendezvous locations, and status updates about "The Great War", and seems to describe an EK-class scenario caused by the release of SCP-███.

To read:

The broadcast at 100.2 MHz is apparently a looped recording of survival instructions, rendezvous locations, and status updates about "The Great War", and seems to describe an EK-class scenario caused by the release of SCP-1427.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I rather like the ones we see a bit of information about but I have a problem with 107.9. I understand that you're trying to go for the mysterious creepy factor with all the redacted and the special procedures regarding that particular channel but frankly there isn't enough tangential information about it to make it seem creepy. It mostly just seems like you don't have an idea for what the expungements are and rather think that a deliberate use of redactions will make it creepy for you. Give us a couple hints about what it could be, just hints, it doesn't have to be anything really concrete, and the redactions will give it so much more… Umph!

item.title: Re: EK
item.content:encoded: Honestly, I didn't have any specific "type" of end-of-world/civilization scenario, other than it was progressive & invasive rather than immediate/instantaneous. "Extinction of all human consciousness" works, so long as this particular one was slow. Philosophical zombies or a hive mind, for instance.

I really want to like this. I just can't. So I'm finally downvoting it, because the issues have bugged me every time I've read it.

I don't mind ALL the expunged and redacted stuff, but it stands out as a minus point because there's not enough interesting stuff actually present in the article. item.title: Re: 107.9 MHz
item.content:encoded: I don't see the last broadcast as insanity-inducing, actually. I see it more along the lines of providing certain… information that's very very tempting to exploit on a personal level. They can't really restrict the work exposure of the analysts (it would take too much time/effort to bring new ones up to speed), but they *can* limit the exposure of the translators/interpreters as apparently the language is common enough that there's no shortage of people who can speak/understand it.

item.title: Re: 107.9 MHz
item.content:encoded:
True, but this is the Foundation. We've MUCH worse things then just "people dying horribly" to make you listen to. Things that would be easer to watch - so all you can do is IMAGINE how they look. And the imagination is the biggest fear of all.

And (referring to clipboard) how does that make you feel?

item.title: 107.9 MHz
item.content:encoded:
You know, you could make this psychologically damaging rather than paranormal.

If you've read World War Z, you'll remember the bit about Radio Free Earth and the IR operators. They were forced to listen to emergency broadcasts from all across the globe, and the emotional trauma of listening to so many people dying live on air caused every single one to commit suicide over the course of 10 or so years.

Now an SCP researcher would be a lot tougher than that. But for how long do you think that someone can listen to innocent people dying horribly and remain perfectly fine? The knowledge of their helplessness, the fear that this could happen to them and the constant exposure would result in a need for psychological counselling at the least.

Paranormal's ok too, but there's probably a heap of Insan-O-Broadcasts out there already.

item.content:encoded:
Requirements for an upvote: creepy, very interesting, or very very witty.

Requirements for a dowvote: either none of the above or unforgivable typos/threats to lower to D-class.

This SCP fits neither category. It's somewhat interesting and a little creepy, but not enough of either for an upvote. At the same time, it isn't bad and there is nothing about it that sends up a red flag, so yeah, I'm going to have to say no vote. Yay democracy!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Yeah, I was somewhat worried that people would have this reaction. What I was trying to get at, though, was that the Foundation really, really wants to listen to each of those 4 broadcasts 24/7, but the limitations of the radio won't let them. So they have to compromise with the channel switching, and risk losing valuable data.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The language choices were definitely deliberate. I was envisioning a situtation like you sometimes find in local English/Spanish stations in the American Southwest, where the radio host will be speaking one language or the other and randomly shift to the other without pausing. Basically, the idea is that those broadcasts are coming from an area/reality where both languages are very prominent, to the point that it's assumed that everyone listening is fluent in both. As to why those radically different languages are both that prominent, well, that's up to you.

And thanks for the tip-off about not posting in the announcements thread. I completely forgot.
